extracted.intended_audience: patent applicants and practitioners (patentees, patent attorneys/agents) before the USPTO
extracted.subtask_description: Procedures and substantive standards for requesting reconsideration, reinstatement, or recalculation of Patent Term Adjustment (PTA) under 35 U.S.C. 154(b) and 37 CFR 1.705, including the 'due care' showing, timing, fees, examples, and limitations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Request for reconsideration under 37 CFR 1.705(b) — timing and required contents
rubrics_metrics.description: Any request for reconsideration of the patent term adjustment indicated on the patent must be by way of an application for patent term adjustment filed no later than two months from the date the patent was granted (this two-month period may be extended under 37 CFR 1.136(a)). An application for patent term adjustment under this section must be accompanied by: (1) the fee set forth in 37 CFR 1.18(e); and (2) a statement of the facts involved, specifying: (i) the correct patent term adjustment and the basis or bases under 37 CFR 1.702 for the adjustment; (ii) the relevant dates as specified in §§ 1.703(a) through (e) for which an adjustment is sought and the adjustment as specified in § 1.703(f) to which the patent is entitled; (iii) whether the patent is subject to a terminal disclaimer and any expiration date specified in the terminal disclaimer; and (iv)(A) any circumstances during the prosecution of the application resulting in the patent that constitute a failure to engage in reasonable efforts to conclude processing or examination of such application as set forth in § 1.704; or (B) that there were no circumstances constituting a failure to engage in reasonable efforts to conclude processing or examination of such application as set forth in § 1.704.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The two-month period may be extended under 37 CFR 1.136 for up to five additional months (permitting reconsideration as late as within seven months after grant). The Office will perform a manual redetermination in response to a request for reconsideration. If additional information is required the Office will issue a requirement for information; a renewed request must be filed within two months of that requirement (extendable under 1.136).

rubrics_metrics.name: Reinstatement request under 37 CFR 1.705(c) — timing, fee, and 'all due care' showing
rubrics_metrics.description: Any request for reinstatement of all or part of the period of adjustment reduced pursuant to § 1.704(b) for failing to reply to a rejection, objection, argument, or other request within three months of the date of the mailing of the Office communication must be filed prior to the issuance of the patent. Such a request must be accompanied by: (1) the fee set forth in 37 CFR 1.18(f); and (2) a showing to the satisfaction of the Director that, in spite of all due care, the applicant was unable to reply to the rejection, objection, argument, or other request within three months of the date of mailing of the Office communication notifying the applicant of the rejection, objection, argument, or other request. The Office shall not grant any request for reinstatement for more than three additional months for each reply beyond three months from the date of mailing of the Office communication.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Requests for reinstatement must be filed prior to patent issuance; papers filed after issuance will not be considered. The Office will decide on reinstatement after grant and may issue a certificate of correction if appropriate. The three-month extensions limit (maximum three additional months per late reply) is absolute.

rubrics_metrics.name: Due care standard — meaning of 'in spite of all due care'
rubrics_metrics.description: The statute requires a showing that, 'in spite of all due care,' the applicant was unable to respond within the 3-month period. The 'due care' of a reasonably prudent person standard is invoked and the phrase 'in spite of all due care' indicates a higher degree of care than the ordinary 'unavoidable delay' standard.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants should not rely on decisions interpreting 'unavoidable delay' (35 U.S.C. 133) as controlling. Courts and prior decisions (e.g., In re Mattullath; Ray v. Lehman) describe the inquiry as whether a party exercised the due care of a reasonably prudent person, but the PTA 'all due care' threshold is more exacting. The reinstated PTA is limited to the period demonstrated to be affected despite all due care.

rubrics_metrics.name: Examples of circumstances that may establish 'in spite of all due care'
rubrics_metrics.description: Illustrative showings that may establish inability to respond within three months in spite of all due care include: (A) the original three-month period was insufficient to obtain test data necessary for an affidavit or declaration under 37 CFR 1.132 that was submitted with a reply filed outside the original three-month period; (B) the applicant was unable to reply within the original three-month period due to a natural disaster; (C) the applicant was unable to reply within the original three-month period because testing was required to reply to an Office action, and the testing necessarily took longer than three months; or (D) the applicant was unable to reply within the original three-month period due to illness or death of a sole practitioner of record who was responsible for prosecuting the application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Any reinstated PTA is limited to the period for which the showing establishes that despite all due care the applicant was unable to reply. The Office will examine the factual record to determine the applicable period.

rubrics_metrics.name: Examples of circumstances that will NOT establish 'in spite of all due care'
rubrics_metrics.description: Circumstances that would not establish inability to respond in spite of all due care include: (A) preoccupation with other matters (e.g., an inter partes lawsuit or interference) given priority over prosecution; (B) illness or death of the practitioner where other practitioners in the same firm could have acted; (C) time consumed with communications between the applicant and representative; (D) vacation or other non-attention to the application; (E) filing by first-class mail with certificate of mailing instead of faster permitted methods and the reply not being received within three months; or (F) failure of clerical employees or the applicant's representative to docket or perform other tasks necessary for reply.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These non-examples emphasize that delays within the applicant's or representative's control, foreseeable events without adequate backup, or reliance on slower filing methods are not ordinarily sufficient to meet the 'all due care' standard.

rubrics_metrics.name: Office redetermination outcomes and what follows
rubrics_metrics.description: The Office's manual redetermination in response to a request for reconsideration may: (1) result in the amount requested by the applicant (Office issues a decision granting the request and a certificate of correction indicating the revised PTA); (2) result in the same amount as indicated in the patent (Office issues a decision denying the request for reconsideration); or (3) result in a different amount (Office issues a redetermination explaining how it arrived at the different adjustment).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If a redetermination differs from the patent, the applicant has two months from the date of the redetermination to file a renewed request for reconsideration addressing the redetermination (no additional fee required); the two-month period is extendable under 37 CFR 1.136(a). If the Office issues a requirement for information, the applicant similarly has two months to file a renewed request supplying the information. A decision denying reconsideration is the Director's decision under 35 U.S.C. 154(b)(4).

rubrics_metrics.name: Appeal rights and required sequence before judicial review
rubrics_metrics.description: An applicant dissatisfied with the Director's decision on a request for reconsideration under 35 U.S.C. 154(b)(3) shall have exclusive remedy by filing a civil action against the Director in the United States District Court for the Eastern District of Virginia within 180 days after the date of the Director's decision on the request for reconsideration.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The statutory scheme requires applicants first to request reconsideration under 35 U.S.C. 154(b)(3) and 37 CFR 1.705(b); only after receiving a decision denying that request may the applicant bring the civil action (35 U.S.C. 154(b)(4)). The AIA Technical Corrections Act clarified that the civil action is the exclusive remedy in this context for patents granted on or after January 14, 2013. For patents issued prior to that date, earlier rules applied (and tolling issues may have been litigated).

rubrics_metrics.name: Third-party submissions regarding PTA (37 CFR 1.705(d))
rubrics_metrics.description: No submission or petition on behalf of a third party concerning patent term adjustment under 35 U.S.C. 154(b) will be considered by the Office; any such submission or petition will be returned to the third party or otherwise disposed of at the convenience of the Office.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This implements 35 U.S.C. 154(b)(4)(B) for patents granted on or after January 14, 2013 (and previously under 1.705(f) for patents granted before that date).

rubrics_metrics.name: Optional recalculation procedure for certain international applications (PTA recalculation PTO/SB/132)
rubrics_metrics.description: An optional procedure was provided for patentees to request a recalculation of their PTA without a fee for patents issued between January 14, 2013 and May 20, 2014 that resulted directly from an international application that entered the national stage under 35 U.S.C. 371. Any request under this optional procedure had to be filed no later than July 31, 2014, using form PTO/SB/132. The optional procedure is not applicable to patents that resulted from applications under 35 U.S.C. 111(a), including bypass continuations of international applications or continuations of international applications that entered the national stage under 35 U.S.C. 371.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A recalculation under the optional procedure is not a request for reconsideration under 35 U.S.C. 154(b)(3); it is a new PTA determination. Any subsequent request for reconsideration of that new determination must comply with 37 CFR 1.705(b)(1)-(2) and be filed within two months of the date of the new determination (extendable under 1.136(a)). The optional procedure waived certain timing/fee requirements only for patents meeting the specified criteria and filing deadlines; it did not waive 35 U.S.C. 154(b)(4) civil action rights.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recordkeeping, PAIR/PALM checks, and how dates are treated for PTA calculations
rubrics_metrics.description: Information as to how the PTA calculation has been made will be available through PAIR. Applicants may routinely use PAIR to check the accuracy of the data entered in the PALM system (e.g., type of paper and date of receipt) throughout prosecution. The date that should be recorded in the Office computer records is the date of receipt of the paper, not the date it was mailed under 37 CFR 1.8. If an original paper is misplaced by the Office and a duplicate is filed with a postcard receipt showing the date of receipt of the original paper, the date shown on the postcard receipt for the original paper is the date that should be shown in the Office computer records. If Priority Mail Express® service was used, the date shown as the 'date accepted' on the Priority Mail Express® label will be entered into the Office computer records.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants should check PAIR/PALM and, if errors are detected, bring them to the Office's attention (e.g., contact the examiner or Technology Center customer service representative) as soon as possible to ensure correction before allowance and PTA determination.

rubrics_metrics.name: Certificate of correction requests and PTA revisions must be separate
rubrics_metrics.description: If a request for a certificate of correction would also attempt to revise the patent term adjustment indicated in the patent, the request for a certificate of correction will not be granted unless the patentee submits a new request for a certificate of correction that does not also attempt to revise the patent term adjustment indicated in the patent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not combine a certificate-of-correction request that changes the patent text with an attempt to revise PTA in the same filing; submit separate appropriate requests per the rules for PTA reconsideration or certificate of correction.

rubrics_metrics.name: Three-month reply computation and business-day rules (35 U.S.C. 21(b) applicability)
rubrics_metrics.description: The provisions of 35 U.S.C. 21(b) are applicable to the determination of the three-month period for reply. If the last day of the three-month period falls on a Saturday, Sunday, or federal holiday within the District of Columbia, then action may be taken, or the fee paid, on the next succeeding secular or business day without loss of any patent term adjustment under 37 CFR 1.704(b).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: if the three-month reply period expires on a Saturday and the applicant files a reply received by the Office on the following Monday (not a federal holiday), the reply will be treated as timely for PTA purposes and no PTA reduction will be applied.
